title: Design a URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bit.ly)
subtitle: Base62 encoding, KGS pre-allocation, read-heavy caching & 301 vs 302 redirects
functionalReqs: Given a long URL, generate a globally unique short alias (7 chars from [a-zA-Z0-9]).
Redirect HTTP GET /:code to the original long URL with p99 latency < 20ms.
Support optional custom aliases and link expiration TTL.
Track basic click analytics asynchronously without slowing down redirects.

nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Links are created once and clicked hundreds of times.
Redirects sit on the user's critical page-navigation path.
Broken short links break external emails, QR codes, and social posts.
Two distinct long URLs must never silently overwrite each other.

workedSummary.hotCacheRam: Size by distinct hot links, not reads: ~400M redirects/day might touch ~20M distinct links; caching the hottest 20% (~4M × 500 B) is ~2 GB, so plan ~4–6 GB with Redis overhead

coreEntities.name: KeyLeaseBatch
coreEntities.storageEngine: KGS Unused/Used DB + In-Mem Worker Leases

apiContracts.purpose: Create a short link using KGS or custom alias
Resolve short code and return HTTP 302 (or 301) Location header

explorerTopology.title: URL Shortener Redirect & Creation Flow
explorerTopology.subtitle: Read-through Redis cache + Bloom filter + async click analytics
explorerTopology.overview: Writes fetch pre-generated collision-free Base62 keys from an in-memory KGS lease. Reads hit Redis (or edge cache) first, guarded by a Bloom filter against bogus codes, and emit click events asynchronously to Kafka.
keyTakeaways: 62^7 ≈ 3.52 trillion unique 7-char keys—enough for centuries at 4M links/day.
Use HTTP 302 (Found) when you need server-side click analytics or mutable targets; use 301 only for immutable zero-analytics links.
Pre-generating keys via KGS eliminates write-time hash collision retries.

nodes.label: Browser Client
nodes.summary: User clicking a short URL or submitting a long URL to shorten.
failureModes: Browser permanently caches 301 redirects, preventing later analytics

nodes.label: API Gateway + Rate Limiter
nodes.summary: Terminates TLS, throttles abusive link creators, routes reads vs writes.
failureModes: Unthrottled bot writes exhaust KGS key pool

nodes.label: Redirect & Shorten Service
nodes.summary: Resolves short codes via Cache-Aside and holds leased 1,000-key blocks from KGS.
failureModes: Crash drops unused in-memory key lease (acceptable <0.01% key waste)

nodes.label: Redis Hot Link Cache
nodes.summary: Serves >85% of redirects directly from RAM in <1ms.
failureModes: Random non-existent code scans bypass cache unless Bloom filter guards

nodes.label: Sharded UrlMapping DB
nodes.summary: Durable authoritative mapping partitioned evenly by short_code.
failureModes: Hot viral link hits single DB partition if Redis misses

nodes.label: Analytics Kafka Topic
nodes.summary: Records referrer, geo, and timestamp asynchronously without blocking redirect response.
failureModes: Synchronous DB counter increment on every redirect causes row-lock contention

steps.info: GET /aB9x2Kq arrives at regional API Gateway
steps.inspectorNote: Gateway validates short-code regex `[a-zA-Z0-9]{7}` before forwarding—bad syntax fails at edge.

steps.payloadInspector: REDIS HIT in 0.5ms -> skip DB query completely
steps.inspectorNote: 80%+ of clicks target the top 20% viral/recent links, kept warm in Redis.

steps.info: Fire-and-forget buffered ClickEvent emitted to url.clicks
steps.inspectorNote: Click counting is buffered asynchronously so redirect latency stays under 5ms inside the datacenter.

steps.payloadInspector:
HTTP/2 302 Found
Location: https://systemcraft.dev/hld/roadmap
Cache-Control: private, max-age=0
steps.inspectorNote: 302 ensures repeat clicks hit our gateway for analytics and lets link owners update or expire URLs.

chaosScenarios.title: Viral Link Cold Miss + Bogus 404 Scan Flood
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: 10,000 req/s arrive for bogus random codes AND an expired viral link simultaneously.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: A shared RedisBloom filter (BF.ADD on every create, so new links are visible to every pod) drops bogus codes before the DB; a SET NX refresh lease lets one pod refill the viral link while the rest wait or serve stale.

steps.info: Random scan /zzzz999 rejected by Bloom filter -> instant 404 (0 DB calls)
steps.inspectorNote: Prevents cache penetration attacks from flooding the primary DB. The filter is shared, not per pod: a link created on pod A must be visible to pod B immediately, or fresh links 404.

steps.info: The pod holding the refresh lease runs 1 DB read and restores the Redis entry
steps.payloadInspector: SET refresh:aB9x2Kq NX PX 2000 -> OK -> 1 DB read -> SETEX url:aB9x2Kq 86400
steps.inspectorNote: With a fleet-wide lease the DB sees 1 read. Per-pod Singleflight alone would still send one read per pod.

pros: Predictable non-sequential random codes (prevents URL scraping)
cons: Needs background job to replenish unused key pool
Small key loss if pod crashes mid-lease
Must check DB and salt/retry on prefix collision
Adds extra DB round-trip under load

deepDives.title: 301 Permanent vs 302 Temporary Redirect
deepDives.bottleneck: 301 caches permanently inside browsers, blinding click analytics and preventing expiry updates.
deepDives.solution: Return 302 (or 307) when analytics, A/B routing, or link deactivation matter; reserve 301 for static zero-analytics traffic.
deepDives.tradeoff: 302 increases server QPS compared to 301 browser caching, so Redis + CDN shielding absorb the extra reads.

deepDives.title: Preventing Sequential Scraping & DB Hotspots
deepDives.bottleneck: Auto-increment Base62 IDs (`0000001`, `0000002`) let scrapers enumerate all private links and skew range partitions.
deepDives.solution: Shuffle pre-generated KGS batches or XOR/Feistel-permute counter IDs before Base62 encoding, and hash-partition DB by `short_code`.
deepDives.tradeoff: Random keys reduce B-Tree insert locality slightly on write, acceptable at only 40–120 writes/sec.

criteria: Sizes the hot cache from distinct hot links (a few GB), not raw reads
